newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Krajisnik commits to deal on Karadzic - U.S. envoy.
newsitem.headline: Krajisnik commits to deal on Karadzic - U.S. envoy.

text.p: U.S. envoy Richard Holbrooke said on Saturday that he had won a promise from Momcilo Krajisnik, the Serb member of the Bosnian presidency, to make indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic withdraw from politics.
Holbrooke told reporters that Krajisnik had "offered a unilateral undertaking" to fulfil a July 1996 agreement which Karadzic had "shredded".

Holbrooke was speaking after more than eight hours of meetings on Friday and Saturday with Yugoslav President Slobodan Milosevic. He said the United States would be closely watching to see whether Krajisnik kept his promise.
"Are we satisfied? Of course not. There has been no change on the American position -- indicted war criminals must be brought to justice," he said.

Under a deal Holbrooke brokered last year with Milosevic and Krajisnik, Karadzic stepped down as Bosnian Serb president and was supposed to stay out of politics. But he recently re-emerged as the man pulling all the strings in the Bosnian Serb territory and has engaged in a power struggle with his successor Biljana Plavsic, who accused him of crime and looting.
Holbrooke also told reporters that Milosevic invited all three Bosnian co-presidents, including Croat Kresimir Zubak and Moslem Alija Izetbegovic, to visit Belgrade.
